subject: Polity
description: Solicitor General of India and Additional Solicitors General — appointment, role, hierarchy among government law officers, distinction from Attorney General.

questions.stem: Who APPOINTS the Solicitor General of India?
questions.explanation: The SOLICITOR GENERAL OF INDIA (SG) is appointed by the APPOINTMENTS COMMITTEE OF THE CABINET (ACC) — chaired by the PRIME MINISTER, includes the Home Minister + Minister of Law & Justice. This is DIFFERENT from the ATTORNEY GENERAL (AG), who is appointed DIRECTLY BY THE PRESIDENT (Article 76). KEY DISTINCTION: AG is a CONSTITUTIONAL POST (Article 76); SG and Additional SG are STATUTORY/Government posts (NOT mentioned in the Constitution). HIERARCHY of GOVERNMENT LAW OFFICERS: (1) ATTORNEY GENERAL of India (Art 76) — top-most. (2) SOLICITOR GENERAL of India — second-rank. (3) ADDITIONAL SOLICITORS GENERAL (currently 4-6 positions). (4) ASSISTANT SOLICITORS GENERAL (HCs). (5) Standing Counsels, government counsels at HC/SC. ROLE OF SG: assists the AG, represents the Government of India in important cases, prepares legal opinions on complex government matters. CURRENT SG (as of April 2026): Tushar Mehta (since 2018, longest-serving SG in recent times). PREDECESSORS: Ranjit Kumar (2014-17), Mohan Parasaran (2013-14), Gopal Subramanium (2009-11). TENURE: typically 3 years; renewable. PYQ FREQUENCY: SG-AG distinction is a top UPSC, MPSC polity MCQ — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Solicitor General of India is which RANK among government law officers?

options.option_text: Equal in rank with the AG himself

questions.explanation: GOVERNMENT LAW OFFICERS HIERARCHY: (1) ATTORNEY GENERAL of INDIA (AG) — TOP, constitutional post (Art 76). (2) SOLICITOR GENERAL of INDIA (SG) — SECOND. (3) Additional Solicitors General (ASGs). (4) Assistant SGs (at HC level). KEY ROLE OF SG: ASSISTS the AG; takes the lead in complex constitutional matters. The SG often appears in court when the AG is unavailable or when the case is delegated. STATUS: SG-AG are not in a 'reporting' relationship — both are independent law officers, but in PROTOCOL the AG outranks SG. AG'S STATUS: equivalent to a Cabinet Minister (Art 76); attends Parliament (right of audience) but not a Member; cannot vote. SG: NO right to attend Parliament. EMOLUMENTS: AG draws salary equal to SC judge (~Rs 2.5 lakh/month + perks); SG ~similar but a step lower. CURRENT (2026): AG = R. Venkataramani (since Sept 2022); SG = Tushar Mehta. CASES SG DEFENDED: Article 370 abrogation (Kashmir), CAA, Sabarimala temple-entry case, electoral bonds, Ayodhya verdict assistance. PYQ FREQUENCY: hierarchy of law officers is 1× per UPSC, MPSC, state PSC cycle.

questions.stem: The post of Solicitor General of India is mentioned in which document?

options.option_text: Article 76 of Constitution of India (option here)
Code of Civil Procedure 1908 here (option here)

questions.explanation: The SG and ASGs are governed by the LAW OFFICERS (CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 1987 — a STATUTORY framework, NOT a constitutional one. CONTRAST: ATTORNEY GENERAL is created by ARTICLE 76 of the Constitution (a constitutional post). KEY IMPLICATION: SG can be APPOINTED, SUSPENDED, or REMOVED by the executive (ACC) at its discretion — no constitutional protection. AG, by contrast, is a constitutional post but holds office DURING THE PLEASURE of the PRESIDENT (effectively the Cabinet) — also removable, but historically AG resignation accompanies a change of government. ELIGIBILITY for SG/ASG (per Rules): must be qualified to be a JUDGE of HIGH COURT — ie, advocate of HC for ≥10 years OR has held judicial office for ≥10 years. CONVENTION: SG is usually elevated AG when AG retires (e.g., Mukul Rohatgi, K.K. Venugopal had similar trajectories). LAW MINISTRY: oversees law officers' day-to-day functioning. CURRENT ASGs (2026): N. Venkataraman (revenue/tax cases), Vikramjit Banerjee, Aishwarya Bhati (first woman ASG, 2021), among others. PYQ ANGLE: 'is SG constitutional or statutory?' is a UPSC PT topic — 1× per 2 cycles.

questions.stem: Who is the FIRST and ONLY constitutional law officer mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 76 — only the ATTORNEY GENERAL OF INDIA is mentioned in the Constitution as the first law officer of the Government of India. KEY PROVISIONS of Art 76: (1) President APPOINTS AG. (2) Must be qualified to be a SC judge (ie, citizen, age ≥ 35, HC judge for 5 yrs OR HC advocate for 10 yrs). (3) Holds office during PRESIDENT'S PLEASURE. (4) Receives such REMUNERATION as the President may determine. (5) DUTY: to give legal advice to GOI on matters referred by President; appear in SC on behalf of GOI. (6) Has RIGHT OF AUDIENCE in ALL COURTS in India. (7) MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT-LIKE PRIVILEGES: can take part in Parliamentary proceedings (BOTH HOUSES + committees) but CANNOT VOTE. He's NOT an MP. AG'S RANK: equivalent to Cabinet Minister; precedes State Chief Justices; accompanies PM/President at protocol events. RESTRICTIONS on AG: cannot advise / hold brief AGAINST GOI; cannot accept Cabinet posts; can hold private practice if permitted. CONTRAST WITH ADVOCATE GENERAL (states, Article 165) — analogous role at state level; appointed by Governor. SG/ASG/State Standing Counsels: NOT mentioned in Constitution. PYQ FREQUENCY: AG vs other law officers is a perennial UPSC, MPSC topic.

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides for an ADVOCATE GENERAL at the STATE level?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 165 — provides for an ADVOCATE GENERAL OF THE STATE — analogous to Attorney General at the Central level, but for state governments. KEY PROVISIONS: (1) Appointed by GOVERNOR. (2) Must be qualified to be a HIGH COURT judge. (3) Holds office during GOVERNOR'S PLEASURE. (4) Receives such remuneration as Governor determines. (5) DUTY: legal advice to STATE GOVT on matters referred to him. (6) RIGHT OF AUDIENCE: can address state legislative assembly + committees but CANNOT VOTE. CONTRAST: AG (Centre, Art 76) vs Advocate General (State, Art 165). FUNCTIONALLY analogous; CONSTITUTIONALLY parallel. ADVOCATE GENERAL OF STATE rank: equivalent to State Cabinet Minister. STATE LAW OFFICERS HIERARCHY: (1) Advocate General. (2) Additional Advocates General. (3) Government Pleaders / Standing Counsels. SAMPLE current (2026): different per state. STATE — RECENT TRENDS: many states have started appointing senior counsels with strong constitutional reputations to AG roles, recognizing the need for elite legal representation. KEY DISTINCTIONS — AG of India vs SG: AG = Art 76 constitutional; SG = statutory under 1987 Rules. AG of state (Advocate General) = Art 165 constitutional. PYQ ANGLE: this Article-distinction is a top UPSC, state PSC polity MCQ.

questions.stem: Can the Solicitor General of India have a PRIVATE LEGAL PRACTICE alongside his official duties?

options.option_text: Yes, only in Supreme Court alone
Only with Bar Council prior consent

questions.explanation: Per the LAW OFFICERS (CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 1987 — the SOLICITOR GENERAL of INDIA is generally PROHIBITED from private legal practice while holding office. RESTRICTIONS on SG: (1) Cannot advise or hold brief AGAINST the Government of India in any case. (2) Cannot defend ACCUSED persons in criminal cases (without Govt permission). (3) Cannot accept appointment as a director in any company without Govt permission. (4) Cannot be an active member of a political party. CONTRAST WITH ATTORNEY GENERAL: Art 76 traditionally allowed AG private practice (subject to no conflict-of-interest with GOI), but in practice modern AGs typically don't accept private briefs while holding office. WHY THESE RESTRICTIONS: to PREVENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST between government work and private clients. HISTORICAL CONTEXT: in the early decades of the republic, M.C. Setalvad (first AG) maintained private practice; modern norms have tightened. POST-RETIREMENT: SG/AG often return to elite private practice in Supreme Court — high-value litigation work. KNOWN ELITE LAWYERS post-retirement: Soli Sorabjee, K. Parasaran, Mukul Rohatgi, KK Venugopal — all back in active practice. PYQ ANGLE: rare but appears in HJS exams.

questions.stem: Which is true about the eligibility for APPOINTMENT as Solicitor General of India?

options.option_text: Must be qualified to be HC judge
Must be a former judge of SC
Must have served as MP earlier

questions.explanation: ELIGIBILITY for SG/ASG: must be QUALIFIED TO BE A HIGH COURT JUDGE — per Article 217 (HC judges qualifications): (a) is or has been a judge of a HC for ≥ 5 yrs, OR (b) has been an ADVOCATE of HC (or two HCs in succession) for ≥ 10 yrs. ELIGIBILITY for AG (Art 76): must be qualified to be a SUPREME COURT JUDGE — per Art 124: (a) HC judge for 5 yrs OR HC advocate for 10 yrs OR distinguished jurist (in opinion of President). NOTE: the eligibility criteria for AG and SC judges are SIMILAR; AG is one rung higher in protocol. NO AGE LIMIT specified in the rules for SG (in practice, appointees are typically 50-65). KEY DIFFERENCE FROM JUDGES: AG/SG can be re-appointed; judges generally cannot be reappointed after retirement (unless ad hoc, Art 128). FAMOUS PRACTITIONERS who became LAW OFFICERS: Sorabjee, Salve, Rohatgi, Venugopal, Tushar Mehta — all came from elite private practice. CASE LOAD: AG/SG handle ~50-100 important cases at any time. SUPPORT: SG draws on the Solicitor General's Office (a team of junior counsels, secretarial staff at Ministry of Law). PYQ FREQUENCY: eligibility specifics are tested 1× per UPSC, MPSC cycle.
